t: Canonical key resolution — Exact Record Retrieval
title: Canonical key resolution — Exact Record Retrieval
description:
Exact record retrieval is the discipline of returning precisely the record a caller asked for — by primary key, canonical identifier, or stable locator — and refusing to substitute a summary, a near-match, or a regenerated approximation. In near-boundless archives, summaries drift from sources; the exact-record contract keeps citations grounded, reproducible, and legally defensible. The technique pairs a canonical key space with a fast primary index, a tombstone-aware existence check, and a byte-faithful read path from storage to caller.

This record documents the canonical key resolution approach: Map aliases, legacy IDs, and human-readable names to one canonical record key before any fetch, so duplicate identities never split an archive.

Teaching ladder rank 1 (foundations): this record explains the core idea in plain terms — what inputs the tool takes, what outputs it produces, and when it is the right choice for an archive task.
